person.name: Valerio Di Zio
person.role: Software Developer · Python, Cloud & Data Integration

profile: Software developer with over a year at Go Reply building Python/FastAPI services and cloud integrations on Google Cloud, and earlier the Angular frontend of an Industry 4.0 data dashboard. I work directly with the people who use what I build, from requirements and demos to troubleshooting and support.

MSc in Computer Science and Engineering, 110/110 cum laude, University of Bologna (2025). For my thesis I built most of FairLib, an open-source fairness library published on PyPI and used in the EU AEQUITAS project.
Based in Cesena and available on-site. English B2.

details: Design and build Google Cloud solutions for clients, from requirements and proofs of concept to architecture choices.
Develop Python/FastAPI services for serverless applications, data processing and cloud integrations.
Work directly with client stakeholders in requirements gathering, workshops, demos and feedback cycles, and take part in technical decisions.
Contribute to CI/CD, IAM, monitoring and logging; handle troubleshooting and technical support.
experience.team: Team of 5: developers, architects and a PM

details: Designed and taught four introductory courses for learners with no technical background: Excel for school staff, LEGO Mindstorms robotics for a middle school class and Snap! programming for two primary school classes.
experience.team: Course design and teaching on my own

details: Built the Angular (TypeScript) frontend of an Industry 4.0 data visualisation dashboard.
Worked in weekly sprints alongside the backend developer and the PM to integrate the dashboard with the backend APIs, using Git and CI/CD.

projects.name: FairLib
projects.description: Open-source Python library, published on PyPI, for measuring and reducing bias in machine learning models. On top of my supervisor’s initial DataFrame design, I implemented 3 fairness metrics and 6 mitigation algorithms (3 pre-processing, 3 in-processing) for scikit-learn and PyTorch, each with unit tests, documentation and an example notebook. CI tests it on Linux, Windows and macOS with Python 3.10–3.13.
projects.note: On the Adult Income benchmark, Learning Fair Representations narrowed the gap in positive-prediction rates between men and women from 16.5 to 1.3 percentage points, for a 2-point accuracy cost. Used in the EU AEQUITAS project, where I am a credited contributor to a Zenodo research dataset.
projects.team: MSc thesis · main author, supervised by my advisor

projects.name: PositionPal
projects.description: In a group project I built the Kotlin microservice for user registration and profiles, with hexagonal architecture. I integrated it with the other services through gRPC and RabbitMQ adapters, covered it with integration tests and contributed to the CI/CD pipeline.
projects.team: Team of 3 · I owned the user service

projects.name: NesGen
projects.description: An experiment in teaching a model to compose NES-style music, the sound of old-school video games. I explored Transformer and GAN approaches on the NES-MDB dataset, with MIDI tokenization and fine-tuning.

projects.name: Scooby
projects.description: A web crawler and scraper in Scala 3, with an internal DSL for navigation, extraction and export. Concurrent execution is handled with Akka Typed.
projects.team: Team of 4 · I built the crawler
